transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-13
Time: 15:00 - 16:02 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Ria Patel (LatticeCare Head of Platform), Markus Vogel (LatticeCare MLOps), Tanya Reed (LatticeCare Security), Evan Li (LatticeCare Product)
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recording/ff-20261113-latticecare-01 (placeholder)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to handoff the activation playbook and align on private deployment choices, SSO/KMS requirements, expected throughput/latency, and pilot criteria. Agreed on next steps: Redwood to send playbook & runbook drafts; customer to share SSO metadata, traffic traces; schedule technical install walkthrough.

Topics:
- Deployment mode: Dedicated vs. Private(VPC)/on-prem
- Security: SSO, KMS, audit logs, SOC2 expectations
- Performance: latency SLOs, batching, KV cache behavior
- Runbook: canary rollout, observability, rollback criteria
- Integration: model registry, CI for model rollouts, feature flags

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is maya from redwood inference, i'll run through a very short agenda, and then we'll handoff to diego for the technical checklist, cool?
[00:12] Ria Patel: yeah sounds good, thanks maya. quick note, we have a hard go-live window in Q1 and need to line up infra early.
[00:20] Diego Alvarez: hi all, diego here — se on the redwood side. i'll focus on the activation runbook, private deployment options, and the perf benchmark plan. some of the names in the playbook might be different — we call our dedicated offering "Redwood Dedicate" in older docs, apologies, it should read Redwood Dedicated.
[00:36] Markus Vogel: no worries. first question, we're mostly leaning private/vpc for data residency, but curious about the tradeoffs vs dedicated. what do you recommend?
[00:46] Maya Chen: good question — dedicated is fast to spin up if you can use our managed infra, it gives reserved capacity and simpler ops; private/vpc gives you customer-managed networking and full control of egress, compliance. for latticecare it sounds like private makes sense given the regs you mentioned.
[01:05] Tanya Reed: yes, data residency + encryption at rest is mandatory. we also need KMS/HSM integration and the ability to have audit logs pushed to our SIEM. is that supported in private deployments?
[01:16] Diego Alvarez: absolutely — private supports KMS integration and syslog / cloudwatch-style forwarding. small caveat: for on-prem we have a slightly different agent for log forwarding, we call it the rendezvous collector in internal docs, sometimes transcribed as "Rendavous" in older notes. you'll get a runbook for that.
[01:35] Evan Li: can you say more about model rollouts? we have an internal model registry and CI pipeline, we want blue-green or canary staged rollouts.
[01:43] Diego Alvarez: yes — rollout is controlled at the control plane level, we support canary percents, A/B routing and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. it integrates with webhook notifications and you can pin model versions. the runbook shows a standard canary: 5%, 25%, 100% over morning windows.
[02:05] Ria Patel: on performance — our primary requirement is p99 latency < 300ms for short-chit chat completions, but we also have long context batches. how does redwood handle batching and kv cache?
[02:16] Diego Alvarez: runtime does continuous batching and KV cache prefixing; for short completions we recommend small batch windows and enabling prefix caching. note that quantization may change latency profile; we'll propose a quantization profile for your M60 class hardware. also we sometimes call KV cache "key-value cash" in transcripts — ignore that.
[02:38] Markus Vogel: we run on a mixed fleet (NVIDIA M60 and A100 on prem) — any special kernel or compilation concerns?
[02:45] Diego Alvarez: runtime will select kernels based on architecture. for hybrid fleets we suggest grouping similar hw behind a pool and route by policy. i'll add kernel mapping to the sizing doc.
[03:05] Tanya Reed: SOC2 is in flight but we need to know what evidence redwood will provide for audit: mapping of auth flows, encryption key lifecycle, and access logs.
[03:16] Maya Chen: we can provide SOC2 mapping docs, our control matrix, and we offer per-request audit logs in private. i'll attach our compliance pack.
[03:30] Evan Li: do you support SAML/SCIM? we want SSO + automated provisioning.
[03:34] Diego Alvarez: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported. for private customers we request SSO metadata and SCIM attributes ahead of time. also note some customers call it SSO/SAML interchangeably and the metadata fields differ.
[03:53] Ria Patel: regarding cost — we'd like to understand unit economics: tokens per request, batching savings, and break-even for dedicated vs private.
[04:02] Maya Chen: we will share a sample cost model with batching scenarios. generally batching + prefix cache reduces token cost by 15-40% depending on prompt reuse.
[04:18] Markus Vogel: i want to run our own benchmarks. what's the recommended approach and sample payloads?
[04:24] Diego Alvarez: we'll send a benchmark plan — include representative traffic traces, token lengths, concurrency targets. we recommend starting with a 10-minute steady-state run at your expected qps then a ramp test.
[04:44] Evan Li: any gotchas for model artifacts? we host models in an internal registry and want to point redwood to pull images; what's the supported flow?
[04:52] Diego Alvarez: we support pulling from private registries via auth tokens or using an S3-style model store; if you want repository sync we can do a scheduled pull. i'll put the supported artifact layouts in the runbook.
[05:07] Ria Patel: about observability — we need per-route latency, token breakdown, error traces, and per-tenant quotas. how granular are your dashboards?
[05:18] Maya Chen: console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level breakdowns and traces. for private installs we can export metrics to your prometheus/grafana stacks. dashboards are templated and we'll share an onboarding dashboard pack.
[05:36] Tanya Reed: for legal, do you have a recommended data retention policy or will that be configurable? we need to disable retention by default.
[05:44] Maya Chen: retention is configurable — by default hosted keeps short-term logs for analytics. in private you control retention and we can disable storage of raw prompts if required.
[06:00] Markus Vogel: small nit — earlier you mentioned "Redwood Dedicate", you meant "Dedicated" right? just want to be sure in our docs.
[06:06] Diego Alvarez: yes — "Dedicated". apologies for the slip, old names.
[06:15] Evan Li: if we want a pilot, what's a typical scope and timeline?
[06:19] Maya Chen: typical pilot is 4-8 weeks: week 0 onboarding + infra prep, week 1-2 test deploy + benchmark, week 3 validation with sample traffic, week 4 decision & go/no-go. we can compress if you have internal resources.
[06:36] Ria Patel: for go/no-go success criteria we'll want reliability (99.9% uptime during pilot), p99 latency <300ms for short completions, and security sign-off.
[06:46] Maya Chen: sounds good. we'll include a pilot SLA doc with acceptance criteria.
[07:00] Diego Alvarez: last technical note — when you run benchmarks include burst patterns, and please send sample traces rather than synthetic single-token prompts, real-world prompts help tuning.
[07:12] Markus Vogel: noted, i'll extract some traces from prod.
[07:20] Tanya Reed: one thing on KMS — we would prefer envelope encryption with our key in HSM; does that pattern work?
[07:27] Diego Alvarez: yes, we support envelope encryption with customer KMS; HSM-backed keys are fine. we'll add the KMS flow diagram to the security appendix.
[07:40] Evan Li: any known limitations for function calling or tool invocation in private mode? we use some internal tools for retrieval-augmented generation.
[07:49] Diego Alvarez: function calling works; you need network routing to your tool endpoints or a webhook proxy. if you want offline tools we recommend using a secure egress proxy that we document in the runbook.
[08:05] Ria Patel: okay, recap and owners?
[08:10] Maya Chen: recap: we will share activation playbook + runbook draft (Maya), diego sends sizing & kernel mapping, tanya shares SSO metadata, markus sends traffic traces. next meeting: technical runbook review with infra team — propose 2026-11-23 14:00 UTC.
[08:32] Evan Li: works for me.
[08:35] Tanya Reed: yes.
[08:40] Markus Vogel: fine.
[08:44] Maya Chen: great — thanks everyone. i'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.

(Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and truncated words as is typical from auto-transcript; speaker turns occasionally labeled generically in raw exports.)

End of meeting.
